transcript: Hello everyone, I'm Bruce Carlson of the AARP Washington State Office in Seattle, and this is the AARP Washington State Podcast, where we talk about health, wealth, and self and living your best life after age 50. Today, we're talking about an historic victory for everyone who takes prescription drugs, the recently passed Inflation Reduction Act. The act contains many provisions AARP has long fought for, including allowing Medicare to negotiate drug prices, a cap on insulin costs, and out-of-pocket expenses, and more. We get into it today with our Washington Congresswoman, Pramila Jayapal. Representative Jayapal has served Washington's seventh district since 2017. Her district includes Seattle and Burian, plus Vashon Island, Normandy, Park, Edmund, Shoreline, and Lake Forest Park. This program is a tele-town hall hosted by AARP Washington State Advocacy Director, Kathy McCall. And we take listener questions for the Congresswoman. There's a lot to cover, so let's get into it with U.S. Representative, Pramilla Jayapal.

In addition to that, the Build Back Better plan would have created a national comprehensive paid family and medical leave program, which would have allowed workers to receive partial wages to take time to care for an ill loved one. But I want you to know that we have accomplished historic wins with the Inflation Reduction Act. And with just a couple more Democratic senators, we could finish the job off in the next Congress and pass the rest of the Build Back Better Act. There's so much that can be done to support our aging Washingtonians. And what I want you to know is I am 150% committed to that fight, to protecting the benefits that you have and expanding them and to making sure that we allow our seniors to not just survive, but actually to thrive. So thank you for having me. And I look forward to answering your questions on the Inflation Reduction Act and to hearing your personal stories. Thanks so much, Kathy.
